In Adams, Massachusetts, 4 candidates (W through Z) are running in an election with a single winner. There are 7 voters (A through G) who each rank the candidates from 1 to 4, with 1 meaning first choice and 4 meaning last choice. Those rankings are shown below. Each column represents a single voter's ranking.

A B C D E F G
candidate W 1 3 4 4 1 3 1
candidate X 3 1 2 3 2 2 4
candidate Y 4 4 1 2 4 4 3
candidate Z 2 2 3 1 3 1 2

A Condorcet winner would win in a head-to-head election against any other candidate. Who is the Condorcet winner? (Or, possibly, there is none.)

Consider every head-to-head election. With 4 candidates, there will be \({4\choose 2 }= 6\) pairings (see combinations).

Compare candidates W and X.

So, X beats W.

Compare candidates W and Y.

So, W beats Y.

Compare candidates W and Z.

So, Z beats W.

Compare candidates X and Y.

So, X beats Y.

Compare candidates X and Z.

So, Z beats X.

Compare candidates Y and Z.

So, Z beats Y.

Organize all this into a winner table.

Notice Z wins against all other candidates. Thus Z is the Condorcet winner.

In Adams, Massachusetts, 4 candidates (W through Z) are running in an election with a single winner. There are 7 voters (A through G) who each rank the candidates from 1 to 4, with 1 meaning first choice and 4 meaning last choice. Those rankings are shown below. Each column represents a single voter's ranking.

A B C D E F G
candidate W 2 3 4 2 1 1 4
candidate X 3 1 2 3 3 2 3
candidate Y 1 2 3 4 4 4 2
candidate Z 4 4 1 1 2 3 1

A Condorcet winner would win in a head-to-head election against any other candidate. Who is the Condorcet winner? (Or, possibly, there is none.)

Consider every head-to-head election. With 4 candidates, there will be \({4\choose 2 }= 6\) pairings (see combinations).

Compare candidates W and X.

So, W beats X.

Compare candidates W and Y.

So, Y beats W.

Compare candidates W and Z.

So, W beats Z.

Compare candidates X and Y.

So, X beats Y.

Compare candidates X and Z.

So, Z beats X.

Compare candidates Y and Z.

So, Z beats Y.

Organize all this into a winner table.

No candidate wins against every other candidate. There is no Condorcet winner.

In Adams, Massachusetts, 5 candidates (V through Z) are running in an election with a single winner. There are 7 voters (A through G) who each rank the candidates from 1 to 5, with 1 meaning first choice and 5 meaning last choice. Those rankings are shown below. Each column represents a single voter's ranking.

voter A voter B voter C voter D voter E voter F voter G
candidate V 1 3 4 4 4 2 3
candidate W 4 1 5 3 3 1 1
candidate X 3 2 2 1 1 3 4
candidate Y 2 4 1 2 5 4 2
candidate Z 5 5 3 5 2 5 5

A Borda winner is a candidate that gets the most Borda points, where each voter's ranking gives 0 points to the last choice, 1 point to the next lowest, etc.

How many Borda points would candidate V get from all 7 voters combined?

There are 5 candidates. So, we subtract each preference number from 5 to get Borda points. We then add all the Borda points from each voter.

In Adams, Massachusetts, 4 candidates (W through Z) are running in an election with a single winner. There are 11 voters (A through K) who each rank the candidates from 1 to 4, with 1 meaning first choice and 4 meaning last choice. Those rankings are shown below. Each column represents a single voter's ranking.


Who would win an instant-runoff election?

First, there are 11 voters, so a candidate needs at least 6 votes to win a majority.

Nobody has a majority. Candidate W has the fewest votes. Eliminate candidate W from the contest. Each voter's vote goes to their top candidate still in the election.

Nobody has a majority. Candidate Y has the fewest votes. Eliminate candidate Y from the contest. Each voter's vote goes to their top candidate still in the election.

Candidate Y has gotten majority vote. Candidate Y wins!
